newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller in corruption ruling next week.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller in corruption ruling next week.

text.p: A parliamentary commission will rule next week on sending Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, to the Supreme Court on corruption charges, MPs said on Thursday.
"We will meet on Monday at 1030 (0830 GMT) and not break up until we have reached a final decision," commission head Metin Bostancioglu told reporters. A ruling had been expected on Thursday.

The body must decide whether to ask parliament to send Ciller to the highest court in the land on charges that she failed to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company during her recent tenure as prime minister.
The government has a majority of one MP in the 15-member commission.

Ciller, now also the foreign minister, headed three governments from 1993 until earlier this year. She now serves in coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan whose Welfare Party had previously backed the allegations.
